comments.body:
@taksmon: a heads-up about a new required check on `main`, `android-line`, added in #433. Any PR that touches `ios/`, `wattracker/cloud/` or `tests/vectors/` now needs this line in its description:

```
Android: <...> #N
```

Alternatively, `Android: n/a <reason>` passes too. This PR changes `tests/vectors/cloud_objects_v1.json`, so the check applies. The check runs when you next push or edit the description, so adding `Android: #196` to the description is enough. No code change is needed.

The reason for the check is in `docs/mobile-parity.md`. That file is now the single place that tracks iOS↔Android parity: a behaviour-by-behaviour matrix, plus the shared vectors (`calendar_grid_v1`, `pairing_code_v1`, `removal_decision_v1`) that the Swift and Kotlin tests both read. Once this PR lands, `removal_decision_v1.json` is the vector your `removeDevice()` rule should be tested against.

Thanks for the careful review. All eight are addressed in `896cba5` + `bde5d3d` (pushed). Per concern:

**1. No-data "waking" state was a dead-end spinner** — Added **pull-to-refresh** to the shared `ScrollableScreenScaffold` (iOS parity). A pull calls the new `DashboardViewModel.pullToRefresh()`, which lifts a cold-start's gate via `retryNowIfWaking()` and re-runs the walk — so `retryNowIfWaking`/`mayBeWaking` now have a real caller in `src/main`. The no-data waking card is a **static notice** (title + `dashboard_waking_notice`), not a spinner that never resolves: nothing is in flight, so a spinner would lie. (`Panel.kt`, `DashboardScreen.kt`, `DashboardViewModel.kt`)

**2. Previous identity's tiles survived a re-pair** — `load()` now tracks `shownIdentity` and clears `dashboardData` the moment the identity changes, before the cache/fetch. A first load that fails no longer leaves the previous rider's tiles up under "Syncing", and the rides carried into the fresh snapshot are this identity's. (`DashboardViewModel.kt`)

**3. Dropped-connection arm of `isColdStart` over HTTPS** — `isColdStart` now walks the cause chain (8-hop limit) and `isDroppedConnection` matches `EOFException`, a `SocketException` that is **not** a `ConnectException`, and `SSLException`. A reset over HTTPS (top-level `SSLException`, or the cause of the thrown `IOException`) is recognised on the wake's first request; a refused connection stays offline. (`CloudSession.kt`)

**4. Refresh retry not lifecycle-guarded** — `performRefresh` re-checks `isCurrent(...)` **inside the cold-start retry closure** (never re-sign a refresh for a departed device) **and again before `noteColdStart()`/`noteFailure()`** (never bank a gate/failure against the departed identity) — the same two checks iOS does. (`CloudSession.kt`)

**5. Four changes not pinned by a test** — each mutation is now caught:
- `retryNowIfWaking()` lift → `aColdStartGateIsLiftableByTheRidersPull` (positive: the pull clears the gate and a request goes out)
- `isWaking` → `aWakingFailureShowsTheWakingNoticeWithNoError`
- deadline throwing plain `IOException` → `aResponseThatOutrunsTheDeadlineIsCutOff` now asserts `SocketTimeoutException` (a bare `IOException` would be read as offline)
- identity re-check before the cache paint → `aSignOutDuringTheCachedReadIsNotPainted` now parks the network step on a gate and asserts the stale cache did **not** paint mid-flight, not just the final state

Plus `aRePairClearsThePreviousIdentitysTiles` (#2) and the #3/#4 cases. (`CloudSessionTest.kt`, `CloudTransportTest.kt`, `DashboardViewModelTest.kt`)

**6. Connect timeout 15s→60s dead-network cost** — the `CONNECT_TIMEOUT_MS` comment now records the trade-off explicitly: a dead network burns the full 60s and is reported as "waking" (a timeout and a wake are indistinguishable here), and this is **iOS parity, not a regression** — the read app is the one that scales, so the wake is the case to size for. (`CloudTransport.kt`)

**7. `cached()` checks then reads without revalidating** — `cached()` captures the identity under the lock, reads the disk off-thread, then **re-checks the identity under the lock before returning**, so a sign-out/re-pair landing in the read window (its disk wipe not yet run) can't hand back the departed identity's rows. (`CloudSession.kt`)

**8. Docs / hygiene**
- **(a)** PR body: 159 → 174; "a refresh cancels the load in flight" → "a refresh under a changed identity cancels the load in flight; a same-identity resume joins it"; the mutation table now names `aChangedIdentitySupersedesTheLoadInFlight`. Same corrections in `plan.md`.
- **(b)** `b18a69b` is reworded to mention the "Agent tooling notes" section it adds to `plan.md`.
- **(c)** `Failure.Waking`'s message no longer duplicates `dashboard_waking_notice` (it's now the short internal reason only), so the screen shows the string resource — the fallback is gone, not merely unreachable.

**Verification:** `:app:testDebugUnitTest` **174 passed, 0 failed** (was 165); `:app:assembleDebug` green.

@taksmon: approved at `bde5d3d`. This one is **yours to merge** whenever you are ready; we will not merge it on your behalf. The numbered points in the review are optional follow-ups, not merge blockers.
